newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary payout hopes drive to new high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary payout hopes drive to new high.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian chemicals firm TVK Rt rose over three percent to a record trading high in early Wednesday trading on expectations that a payout from the state was imminent.
"Everybody takes this for granted," one trader said.
TVK hit 3,330 forints before dropping back by 0950 GMT to 3,320, up 120. The closing record is 3,255 set on June 18.

TVK shares have been heading upwards recently on market expectations that the government privatisation agency APV will decide today on paying out some billion forints plus another one billion in interest to TVK.
A 1989 law promised state-owned companies which transformed themselves into shareholder companies before 1992 that they would receive 20 percent of all subsequent privatisation revenues.
An APV official on Wednesday confirmed to Reuters Monday's information that the payouts were not on the preliminiary agenda of APV's board meeting today.
"But the agenda may change at the last minute," she said, adding that the board has already started its meeting.
APV will hold a news conference about its decision at 1300 GMT.
